tools.name: save_brief
tools.description:
The brief kept, on the reader's yes: their active record, its lanes drawing their own edition from the next
morning. Refused when the record changed since its `confirm`.

tools.name: my_brief
tools.description:
The brief the reader holds, with its plain-language read-back and the `confirm` an amendment saves on; or what
stands in its place.

tools.name: amend_brief
tools.description:
The whole brief as amended by one sentence of the reader's, compiled as set_brief does, with `changes`
against the one they hold. save_brief with the new `confirm` keeps it.

tools.name: forget_brief
tools.description:
The reader's brief dropped, only when they asked for that in words: nothing draws their morning but the
world's. Their history stays on the site.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "news" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: why, delivery · Private data: set_brief, answer_brief, save_brief, delivery · Public sink: why · Destructive: story.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: why, delivery · Private data: set_brief, answer_brief, save_brief, delivery · Public sink: why · Destructive: story

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "morning" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
